messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate observed in /v1/generate across prod-canary (us-west-2). SLO error budget burn > 10% in 5m. Paging oncall: maria (pager duty) :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): acked. looking now. which deploy is this?

kevin (release): rolling canary for feature/fast-batching at 1723UTC. started canary at 1728. only ~10% of traffic.

maria (oncall): seeing spike in 5xx in the canary nodes. dashboards for canary latency are missing; I only have the service-level charts. anyone have the canary-specific grafana link? :confused:

tara (sre): ugh, we forgot to add the canary tag to the dashboard variables in the last refresh. open grafana, search "fast-batching"? I can try to pull the logs.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout id=rel-2026-03-01-1723 status=IN_PROGRESS hostpool=canary-gpu

kevin (release): confirming: release included a batching micro-optimization + new KV cache key format. no infra changes.

maria (oncall): logs show TLS handshake errors 502 from canary proxy to runtime on two hosts. repeated timeouts after 30s.

ahmed (support): getting multiple customer reports - some tenants seeing failed completions and retries. CS has queued a priority email. Sam, FYI.

sam (product): thanks, Ahmed. any indication of which customers? should we hit the kill-switch?

maria (oncall): two immediate ops actions: 1) hold the rollout 2) if noisy / escalating -> rollback or kill flag. But need confirmed impact window and which feature flag controls batching.

kevin (release): flag is ff.fast_batching.enabled in LaunchDarkly. Canary was flipped by the rollout script. I can revert the LD flag in 30s.

maria (oncall): before flipping, can someone confirm metric backfills? Our alerting is noisy: we got duplicate alerts from cloudwatch and datadog for the same symptom; it's possible we're chasing alert storm. Also canary-specific traces not coming through.

tara (sre): confirmation: traces not arriving because the canary pods lacked the tracing env var due to a templating bug. That explains missing traces for the canary. I'll patch and re-instrument but that's not immediate.

kevin (release): proceeding to kill flag now. Rolling back in LaunchDarkly for all canary targets.

devops-bot: action=feature_flag_toggle rel-2026-03-01-1723 flag=ff.fast_batching.enabled target=canary result=SUCCESS by kevin

maria (oncall): after flag toggle, error-rate dropping on the main service-level chart from 12% -> 3% in 90s. Good sign.

ahmed (support): started notifying impacted customers with ETA 30m. attaching temporary workaround steps for SDK users (retry/backoff tweak).

kevin (release): temporary rollback of the canary is in effect; I'm pausing the global rollout. We will not promote until we root cause.

maria (oncall): note: our SLO/alerting playbooks triggered a P1 page but we had no distinct canary dashboard so it was harder to prove isolated impact. Need to log that as an observability gap.

sam (product): customer impact: about 7 tenants saw increased error rates, one enterprise tenant reported 4 failed batch jobs. We should prioritize communication and a postmortem with RCA and mitigation timeline.

tara (sre): quick RCA notes so far: regression likely from KV key format change causing proxy timeouts under certain request sizes; combined with missing tracing on canary and missing canary metrics in grafana made root cause detection slower. Also alerts duplicated across providers caused signal noise and confusion about severity.

maria (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline for 15m break. Tara, you take on-call for followups; kevin, keep the rollback paused. If errors climb >5% reopen paging.

maria (oncall): assigning action items in thread: 1) Tara: create canary grafana dashboard template + add to infra repo. 2) Dev: add tracing env var check to rollout preflight. 3) Platform: dedupe alerts across cloudwatch/datadog for the same metric. 4) Release: run a canary-only test harness for KV key format.

tara (sre): acking handoff. I'll create a ticket and link here: https://internal.redwood/tickets/INC-2026-314 (placeholder).

kevin (release): i'll add a rollback job to the CI to auto-flip LD flags if 5xx > 5% for 2m during canary. will open PR.

devops-bot: incident-note created id=INC-2026-314 created_by=maria severity=P1

ahmed (support): CS message drafted and sent to impacted tenants. will attach transcript and affected request IDs.

maria (oncall): final notes before break: observed impact window ~1728-1736 UTC, mitigated by flag toggle at 1732. Estimated customer-visible failures ~4-6 minutes for impacted sessions. Postmortem owners: Tara (SRE), Kevin (release), Maria (oncall) as reviewer.

sam (product): thanks team. postmortem should include cost/latency numbers, customer list, and plan to prevent similar in next 2 weeks.

tara (sre): logging followups in INC-2026-314. will include a runbook addition about missing canary dashboard detection.

maria (oncall): back. everything looks stable. closing the page for now but keep monitoring for 2 hours. :white_check_mark:

kevin (release): lesson learned: standardize canary env checks in release template. PR inbound.

ahmed (support): CS follow-up scheduled for tomorrow with customers.

incident-bot: incident INC-2026-314 status=MONITORED participants=[maria (oncall), tara (sre), kevin (release)]

maria (oncall): thread summary: canary rollout caused 5xx spike due to KV key format change -> proxy timeouts on canary nodes. Missing canary-specific dashboards and missing tracing env var slowed triage. Duplicate alerts caused signal noise. Mitigated by toggling feature flag and pausing rollout. Action items assigned and ticket created.

kevin (release): adding a note to the release checklist: "verify canary metrics + tracing + LD flag scoped correctly"

tara (sre): will run a postmortem doc and ping stakeholders.

sam (product): filing comms to customer success and account teams now.

ahmed (support): closing CS incident once customers confirm stable.

maria (oncall): closing thread. thanks all. :pray:
